claims.quote: which we have previously shown to result in intracellular accumulation of mutant GABAA receptor γ2(Q390X) subunit protein.
we have here identified an ERAD-associated E3 ubiquitin ligase, HRD1, among other ubiquitin ligases, as a strong modulator of wildtype and mutant γ2 subunit expression.
Overexpressing HRD1 or knockdown of HRD1 dose-dependently reduced the γ2(Q390X) subunit.
zonisamide (ZNS)-an antiseizure drug reported to upregulate HRD1-reduces seizures in the Gabrg2+/Q390X mouse.
a possible mechanism for this effect is a partial rescue of surface trafficking of GABAA receptors
which are otherwise sequestered in the ER due to the dominant-negative effect of the γ2(Q390X) subunit.
this partial rescue was not due to changes in ER chaperones BiP and calnexin, as total expression of these chaperones was unchanged in γ2(Q390X) models.
ZNS alters protein trafficking, providing further support for the use of proteostasis regulators for the treatment of genetic epilepsies.
